A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, retaining the central learning rule, main convergence theorem and original figures. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figures 2 and 5 report original stochastic simulations, including trajectories and Frobenius-error behavior under different learning rates.

after.justification: The original simulations remain, and Figure 6 adds correlated-input simulations. These qualify as original results despite the checklist describing the figures as illustrations.

M1.justification: The original rule and Algorithm 1 remain. Section 5 adds time-varying intensities and a correlated-input model replacing B(k) with C(k)B(k). Appendix A.5 introduces sequential learning periods, projection and removal of previously selected directions in Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: Figure 6 extends the synthetic three-neuron evaluation to correlated inputs with three correlation matrices. The winner-selection task remains. The time-varying-intensity and sequential-learning extensions receive theoretical treatment without additional reported simulations.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated external baselines. Algorithm 2 is introduced theoretically, without an empirical comparison against Algorithm 1; the expanded related-work citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figures 2 and 5 retain their experimental settings. Figure 6 reuses Figure 2's three-neuron trajectory protocol: 2,000 iterations, learning rate 0.01 and uniform noise on [-1,1]^3. Its new correlation conditions change input coverage without a separate protocol or metric revision.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a limited sensitivity analysis showing trajectories and gradient fields under three correlation patterns. The existing initialization illustrations and learning-rate analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions display 100-trajectory simulations, and Figure 6 follows that existing practice. No new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are supplied.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds simulated trajectories and flow patterns for three correlated-input conditions, showing correlation-dependent attraction behavior. Figures 2 and 5 retain their results, including the multiple-output error plateaus. No same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: New material includes the intensity-switching result in Lemma A.5, sequential-alignment results in Appendix A.5, the time-varying ODE derivation in A.6, and correlated-model lemmas and Theorem A.13 in A.7. Existing gradient-flow results are retained after relocation and renumbering. The exponential-variable identity in old Lemma A.5/new Lemma A.7 is corrected from a sum to a minimum.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain STDP as noisy gradient descent, high-probability exponential alignment and the mirror-descent connection. The rewritten abstract emphasizes non-convexity and convergence despite constant noise, properties already asserted in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of correlated learning as PCA restricted to the simplex, time-varying dynamics through replicator fitness, and early priming as a barrier to later adaptation. It replaces the earlier broad online-PCA conjecture with more specific extensions and identifies inhibition, network depth and voltage-dependent STDP as remaining boundaries. The weight-explosion limitation remains.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that illustration code accompanies the submission and will be made public; v1 contains no corresponding disclosure. The PDFs do not establish public code availability or provide additional hardware and execution-time information.

R1.justification: A new Related literature subsection substantially develops positioning against Kempter et al.'s averaged dynamics and STDP derived from energy or information objectives. Ten works are added, including Chechik, Neumann et al. and Surace et al., supporting these distinctions and the discussion of metric choice.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on the abstract, biological motivation and discussion. Related literature gains a dedicated subsection, the explicit two-dimensional solution and gradient-flow lemma move to Appendix A.2, and a checklist is added. The main section sequence and much existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the nine-panel Figure 6 and an Algorithm 2 display. Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, with limited caption, equation-reference and page-reflow changes.

improvement.justification: The correlated-input simulations, expanded positioning and theoretical extensions add useful scope while preserving the original core. However, new technical inconsistencies undermine confidence in those additions: Algorithm 2 loops to d despite specifying K iterations and omits the identity term of Eq. (1); Theorem A.13 prints a self-canceling gap definition and a learning-rate restriction missing epsilon. These verified issues affect substantive new guarantees, so the benefits and reliability costs do not support a confident net quality judgment.
